items.zh: 一个恰当的例证;正是一例
items.en: an example that illustrates the general claim just made
items.example: Regulators tend to arrive after the damage; the three years it took to ban the additive is a case in point.
items.note: 紧接在一般性论断之后引出印证它的实例;比 for example 更强调"正好说明这一点"。

items.zh: 已无实际意义的问题(美);尚有争议的问题(英)
items.en: a question that no longer matters in practice (US), or one that remains open to debate (UK)
items.example: Whether we should have renewed the lease is a moot point now; the landlord sold the building last Thursday.
items.note: 英美分歧最大的短语之一:美式重心是「争不争都没用了」,英式重心是「还没定论,值得争」。两种读法几乎相反,跨大西洋沟通时最好换成 irrelevant 或 debatable。

items.zh: (作介词)在没有……的情况下;若无
items.en: without; in the absence of
items.example: Absent a written agreement from the estate, the auction house will not release the drawings to either brother.
items.note: 学习者只学过形容词「缺席的」,这里是介词,后面直接跟名词,等于 without / in the absence of。美式法律与财经写作高频,语气正式。

items.zh: 临时的;为特定目的临时安排的
items.en: arranged for one particular purpose only, without a general plan
items.example: Flood relief was handled by an ad hoc committee that met four times and was dissolved before the next winter.
items.note: 拉丁语借词,可作形容词或副词;带有"缺乏长期规划"的轻微贬义。

items.zh: 几乎;差不多已经
items.en: almost completely; very nearly
items.example: The bank has all but abandoned rural branches: only nine remain, and six of those now open twice a week.
items.note: 常被按字面误解成"除了……全部";在这个用法里 all but 等于 almost。

items.zh: 更是如此;尤其在……情况下就更是这样
items.en: even more true, for the reason that follows
items.example: Reviewing the contract yourself matters, all the more so when the other side drafted every clause in it.
items.note: so 回指前面整句话,后面常接 when / if / given。写成 all the more 也行,加 so 时前面必须有可回指的整句。

items.zh: 绝不是;根本谈不上
items.en: definitely not; the very opposite of
items.example: The handover was billed as routine, but three servers went offline at once and the night was anything but routine.
items.note: 与 all but 只差一个词,意思却相反:all but routine ≈ 几乎照常,anything but routine = 根本不照常。这一对最容易记混。

items.zh: 严格意义上的;就这个名义而言
items.en: in the strict sense of the word just used; considered in that capacity
items.example: There is no written policy as such, only a memo from 2019 that everyone treats as though it were binding.
items.note: 常被误当成 therefore。本义是"严格说来的那个东西",最典型的框架是 no X as such。

items.zh: 以牺牲……为代价
items.en: with something else suffering as the cost of the gain
items.example: The airline cut turnaround times at the expense of maintenance checks, and the regulator grounded four aircraft in March.
items.note: 表示代价,不是"由某人付钱"(那是 at somebody's expense);后接名词或 -ing。

items.zh: 在边际上;就多加的那一点点而言
items.en: with respect to one additional unit of effort, cost, or supply, rather than the total
items.example: Another hour of testing helps at the margin, but the real defect rate is set by how the specs get written.
items.note: 经济学术语进入了一般评论文章。margin 是「边际」不是「边缘」;它是在说「再多一点点的效果」,常暗示这点效果很小。

items.zh: 预设结论:把有待证明的事当成前提(循环论证)
items.en: to assume as already settled the very point that is in dispute
items.example: Asking why the policy failed begs the question, since the committee has not yet shown that it failed at all.
items.note: 最著名的陷阱:它不是「引出一个问题」。逻辑学 petitio principii 的译名。松散用法(= raises the question)已极其普遍,连报刊也这么写,但在正式论证里用错会被抓。想说「引出问题」就直说 raises the question。

items.zh: 真正的;货真价实的;出于善意的
items.en: genuine and made in good faith, not pretended
items.example: Only bona fide researchers get access to the archive, and each request is checked against a university's own records.
items.note: 法律与正式书面语色彩;作形容词,不要与名词 bona fides(资格证明)混用。

items.zh: 绝非;远远不是
items.en: not at all; far from it
items.example: The recovery is real but by no means secure: two of the three growth drivers depend on a single export market.
items.note: 放句首时主句要倒装 (By no means is this settled);放在 be 动词后则不倒装。

items.zh: 同理;按同样的逻辑
items.en: for the same reason, applying the logic just used to a second case
items.example: If subsidies distort the solar market, then by the same token the fuel-duty freeze distorts the market for diesel.
items.note: 只用于"同一条逻辑推及另一件事",不等于 similarly(那只是"类似地")。

items.zh: 附带的告诫;需要留意的但书
items.en: a warning or condition attached to a statement, limiting how far it holds
items.example: The forecast comes with one large caveat: it assumes the port reopens in April, which nobody in shipping expects.
items.note: 常见搭配 with the caveat that / one caveat;比 warning 更学术,专指限定条件。

items.zh: 事实上的(虽无法律地位)
items.en: existing in fact, though not officially established
items.example: With the assembly suspended for a second year, the governor has become the de facto legislature of the province.
items.note: 与 de jure(法律上的)成对使用;作形容词时不加连字符。

items.zh: 既成事实
items.en: something already done and presented as impossible to reverse
items.example: By the time the committee was consulted the contract had been signed, and members were handed a fait accompli.
items.note: 常搭配 present someone with a fait accompli;强调木已成舟,协商已无意义。

items.zh: 尽管有……;虽然……却
items.en: in spite of; despite the existence of
items.example: For all the money spent on the new ticketing system, passengers still queue at the same two machines every morning.
items.note: 让步用法,等于 despite,不是「为了」也不是「换来」。放句首、后面接名词短语时基本都是这个意思,后半句必有转折。

items.zh: 不知道有没有用,我提一句;姑妄言之
items.en: used to offer information or an opinion while conceding it may not be useful
items.example: For what it's worth, I ran the same query on last year's data and got the identical mismatch.
items.note: 降低姿态的礼貌铺垫,不是真的怀疑自己说的没价值。邮件与技术讨论里常缩写成 FWIW。

items.zh: 要说有什么区别的话,反倒是……
items.en: used to suggest, mildly, the opposite of what was just denied
items.example: The revised figures do not weaken the case for the levy; if anything, they make it harder to argue against.
items.note: 用在否定之后做温和的反向修正,中文很难直译;用对了立刻显得地道。

items.zh: 就其本身而言;单凭这一点
items.en: considered alone, apart from its consequences or context
items.example: A falling birth rate is not, in and of itself, a crisis; what matters is how fast the workforce shrinks around it.
items.note: 多与否定连用;比单说 itself 更强调"孤立地看"。

items.zh: 在很大程度上
items.en: to a considerable degree
items.example: The recovery was in no small part the work of one procurement officer who refused to sign the original contract.
items.note: 双重否定的书面说法,等于 largely;常与 due to / thanks to 连用。

items.zh: 在……之后(紧随某重大事件而来)
items.en: following, and as a consequence of, a major event
items.example: In the wake of the collapse, three regional lenders were forced to disclose how much of the same debt they held.
items.note: 只用于重大或负面事件之后,不能替代普通的 after;后接名词,不接从句。

items.zh: 在……范围内;仅就……而言
items.en: to the extent that; only to the degree that something is true
items.example: The clause binds the contractor only insofar as the delay was within his control, which the flooding clearly was not.
items.note: 正式书面语,尤其常见于法律与学术。它限定范围,不等于 because——译成「因为」就丢掉了「仅在此限度内」的关键含义。英式常拆写成 in so far as。

items.zh: 值得注意的是……
items.en: a marker used to flag a relevant fact the reader might otherwise pass over
items.example: It is worth noting that the survey excluded firms with fewer than ten staff, which is precisely where the job losses landed.
items.note: 常见错误是写成 it is worth to note that;worth 后面必须接 -ing 形式。

items.zh: 更不用说;遑论
items.en: used after a negative statement to introduce something even less likely
items.example: The clinic cannot staff a second nurse, let alone the scanner the regional plan promised it three years ago.
items.note: 前半句必须是否定;后接成分要与前面平行(名词对名词、动词原形对动词原形)。

items.zh: 多半;十有八九
items.en: in most cases, though not always
items.example: Appeals against the assessment succeed more often than not, which tells you something about how the first decision is made.
items.note: 比 usually 更有分寸,暗示"超过一半但并非总是";放句中或句末都自然。

items.zh: 更不用说;遑论
items.en: and certainly not; used after a negative to add something even less likely
items.example: The intern could not find the archive room, much less the 1994 files the partner wanted before lunch.
items.note: 不是「少得多」。必须跟在否定句后面,引出一件更不可能的事,等同 let alone。用在肯定句后是语法错误。

items.zh: 尤其是;其中特别包括
items.en: used to single out one particularly important item from a list
items.example: Several ministers opposed the closure, not least the one whose constituency houses the older of the two plants.
items.note: 不要写成 not the least;意思是"其中尤为重要的是",不是"一点也不"。

items.zh: 尤其是因为;一个很重要的原因是
items.en: used to add a reason that is especially important among several
items.example: The hearing was postponed, not least because the only witness who saw the transfer was still in hospital.
items.note: not least 是曲言法(以否定表强调),意思是「绝非最不重要的」= 尤其。看到 not 就理解成否定原因,是典型误读。

items.zh: 可谓十足的;至少这一点毫无疑问
items.en: used before an adjective to insist that this quality at least is beyond dispute
items.example: The new editor is nothing if not thorough: she read every back issue before changing a single headline.
items.note: 字面像否定,实为强调;后面必须紧跟形容词,不能接名词。

items.zh: 尽管;虽有……(仍然)
items.en: in spite of; without being prevented by
items.example: Notwithstanding two years of record profits, the company froze salaries and told staff the outlook remained uncertain.
items.note: 英语里罕见的可后置介词:the delay notwithstanding 与 notwithstanding the delay 都对,后置更书面。语气比 despite 正式一档。

items.zh: 总的来说;权衡之后
items.en: taking everything into account, after weighing both sides
items.example: On balance the merger should clear, though the regulator will probably force the sale of the two overlapping depots.
items.note: 暗示两边都有道理、权衡后倾向某一边;比 overall 多了"衡量过"这层意思。

items.zh: 表面上看
items.en: judging only from what is immediately apparent, before closer scrutiny
items.example: On the face of it the deal saves the taxpayer money; read the indemnity clause and the liability has simply moved.
items.note: 后面几乎总跟一个转折;比 apparently 更明确地预告下文的反转。

items.zh: 结果却……(引出出乎意料且多半令人失望的后果)
items.en: used to introduce an unexpected and usually disappointing outcome of an action
items.example: She drove four hours to the county office, only to be told the deeds had been moved to a warehouse in Leeds.
items.note: 不是「只是为了」。它标记的是落空:前半句付出努力,后半句被打脸。语气上的意外感是这个结构存在的全部理由。

items.zh: 本身;就其自身而言
items.en: by or in itself, as distinct from its effects or associations
items.example: The tax is not unpopular per se; what voters object to is that the receipts have not reached their own hospital.
items.note: 放在被修饰的名词或形容词之后,不能放前面;多与否定连用。

items.zh: 初步看来(已足以成立的)
items.en: based on first impression, sufficient to proceed with unless later contradicted
items.example: The auditors found a prima facie case of double billing, though nobody had yet traced where the money went.
items.note: 法律拉丁语,现已进入严肃新闻;固定搭配是 prima facie case / evidence。

items.zh: 交换条件;对等的回报
items.en: something given in return for something else, as part of a bargain
items.example: The loan cleared the same week the ministry received the donation, and prosecutors are treating that as a quid pro quo.
items.note: 现在多用于政治与腐败报道,带负面暗示;中性的交换用 trade-off 或 exchange。

items.zh: ……就到此为止了;所谓的……可真行(反讽)
items.en: used to dismiss something as finished or exposed as false
items.example: The heating failed again on the second morning — so much for the landlord's promise that the boiler had been replaced.
items.note: 带明显反讽,宣告某个承诺或说法已被事实推翻。另有一个中性义:演讲中收束话题(So much for the background)。语气全靠上下文区分。

items.zh: 现状;既有格局
items.en: the existing state of affairs, especially one that some party wants preserved
items.example: Every party promised reform, and every party's costed plan turned out to defend the status quo in a different way.
items.note: 几乎总带定冠词 the;暗指"有人从中获益、因而抗拒改变的现状"。

items.zh: 话虽如此
items.en: used to concede a point and then qualify it
items.example: The migration ran three months late; that said, nothing broke on the night, which is more than the last one managed.
items.note: 比 However 轻,承接上一句的让步;书面口语通用,句首后加逗号。

items.zh: 过分地(所修饰的还是优点)
items.en: to an excessive degree, said of a quality that is otherwise a virtue
items.example: He was generous to a fault, lending the deposit to a tenant he had met exactly twice.
items.note: 只修饰褒义形容词且后置;意思是"好过了头",不是"有毛病"。

items.zh: 平心而论;话说回来(引出对对方有利的一点)
items.en: used to introduce a point in favour of the side you have just been criticizing
items.example: To be fair, the vendor warned us about the deadline in April, and we booked the install anyway.
items.note: 是让步标记,不是「公平地说」。后面接的一定是对刚被批评那一方有利的话,所以用错方向会让整段逻辑翻车。

items.zh: 徒劳无功
items.en: without achieving the intended result, despite real effort
items.example: The crew pumped the hold for six hours to no avail, and the ferry settled onto the sandbar before dawn.
items.note: avail 作名词几乎只活在这个短语里;重点是努力过却没用。

items.zh: 说得客气些;这还是轻描淡写
items.en: used to signal that the description just given is a considerable understatement
items.example: The rollout did not go smoothly, to put it mildly; half the branches were offline for nine days.
items.note: 反讽标记:前面说得越轻,实际越严重;位置灵活,句末最常见。

items.zh: 为此;为达成刚说的那个目标
items.en: in order to achieve the aim just mentioned
items.example: The city wants a car-free centre by 2030; to that end, it has already closed four streets around the market.
items.note: end 是古义「目的」,不是「结尾」——所以它绝不表示「最后」。前一句必须已经点明一个目标,否则 that 无处可指。

items.zh: 相对于;就……而言
items.en: in relation to, or compared with
items.example: The euro's weakness vis-à-vis the dollar flattered export earnings and hid a real fall in shipped volumes.
items.note: 法语借词,书面语用于比较关系;口语几乎不用,用多了会显得做作。

items.zh: 事后看来
items.en: judging with knowledge that was not available at the time
items.example: With the benefit of hindsight the warning signs were obvious, but in 2021 the deposit outflows looked entirely seasonal.
items.note: 比 looking back 正式,且明确承认当时并不掌握这些信息,常用于检讨或开脱。

items.zh: 放大版的;同一件事在更大尺度上的重演
items.en: the same thing in a bigger, more obvious, or more extreme form
items.example: The dispute over the parking permits is the city's housing fight writ large, with the same landlords on both sides.
items.note: writ 是 write 的古过去分词,只活在这个词组里。语序特殊:后置修饰名词(X writ large),不能写成 largely written。

items.zh: 双刃剑;利弊并存的事物
items.en: something that has both a clear benefit and a comparable drawback
items.example: Cheap borrowing proved a double-edged sword: it financed the expansion and then made the refinancing cliff impossible to climb.
items.note: 与中文"双刃剑"完全对应,写作时可直接替换掉冗长的 has both advantages and disadvantages。

items.zh: 遮羞布:用来掩饰难堪真相的表面说法或象征性举措
items.en: a token gesture used to cover something embarrassing without changing it
items.example: The pilot program was a fig leaf: forty tablets for a district of nine thousand students, announced the week before the vote.
items.note: 常见搭配 a fig leaf for / of。贬义,且暗示这块布谁都看得穿。

items.zh: 公平竞争的环境
items.en: conditions in which every competitor is subject to the same rules and advantages
items.example: European carriers want a level playing field on state aid before Gulf airlines are granted any more landing slots.
items.note: 贸易与监管报道的固定表达;把"公平竞争环境"直译成 fair competition environment 会很生硬。

items.zh: 惨胜:代价大到得不偿失的胜利
items.en: a win achieved at so high a cost that it is scarcely better than a defeat
items.example: They won the patent suit after four years, but the legal bills and lost customers made it a Pyrrhic victory.
items.note: 源自古希腊国王 Pyrrhus,故首字母大写;读 /ˈpɪrɪk/,与 psychic 无关。

items.zh: 逐底竞争;竞相压低标准
items.en: competition in which rivals keep cutting standards, prices, or wages to undercut each other
items.example: Once one platform waived its commission, the others followed, and delivery pay entered a race to the bottom.
items.note: 经济与监管报道高频;明确的贬义,指标准而非价格的自然下降。

items.headword: a rising tide lifts all boats
items.zh: 水涨船高:整体增长会让所有人受益
items.en: the claim that general economic growth benefits everyone, rich and poor alike
items.example: The minister repeated that a rising tide lifts all boats, but wages in the northern towns had not moved in a decade.
items.note: 政策辩论里的固定引语。注意语用:今天引用它的人多半是为了紧接着反驳它,直接当自己的主张说会显得天真。

items.zh: 一剂强心针;及时的提振
items.en: a sudden boost that revives something that was flagging
items.example: The export licence was a shot in the arm for a shipyard that had not laid a keel since spring.
items.note: 指提振而非治本;后面常接 for + 受益的一方。

items.zh: 不痛不痒的惩罚
items.en: a punishment far milder than the offence deserved
items.example: The bank paid two days' profit in fines, a slap on the wrist that changed nothing about how it lends.
items.note: 重点在"轻得离谱",自带批评意味;不是描述真的打手。

items.zh: 滑坡;开了头就收不住的危险先例
items.en: a course of action likely to lead, step by step, to something much worse
items.example: Critics warned that letting the ministry vet one broadcast licence was a slippery slope towards vetting the news itself.
items.note: 同时也是逻辑谬误 slippery slope argument 的名称,写议论文时常遇到。

items.zh: 铁证;确凿的直接证据
items.en: a single piece of evidence that proves guilt or responsibility beyond argument
items.example: The leaked memo was a smoking gun: it priced the recall six months before the company told the regulator anything.
items.note: 调查报道常用;否定式 no smoking gun 表示"没有找到决定性证据"。

items.zh: 零和博弈;一方所得即另一方所失
items.en: a situation in which one side can gain only as much as the other side loses
items.example: Treating trade as a zero-sum game misses the point that both economies grew fastest when the tariffs were lowest.
items.note: 源自博弈论,现已进入日常评论;最常见于否定句 trade is not a zero-sum game。

items.zh: 全面地;不分对象一律适用
items.en: applying to everyone or everything in a group, without exception
items.example: The chain cut opening hours across the board rather than close the twelve branches that were actually losing money.
items.note: 作定语时要加连字符 (an across-the-board pay rise),作状语时不加。

items.zh: 首当其冲;承受最大的冲击
items.en: to take the worst of an impact when it falls unevenly
items.example: Small suppliers will bear the brunt of the new tariff, since none of them can absorb a nine per cent margin hit.
items.note: 固定搭配 bear the brunt of,定冠词 the 不能省;brunt 单独很少使用。

items.zh: 越界;超出了可以接受的底线
items.en: outside the limits of what is socially or morally acceptable
items.example: Criticizing the proposal is fair; publishing the analyst's home address is beyond the pale, and the forum banned him for it.
items.note: pale 在这里是古义「界桩、辖区边界」,与「苍白」毫无关系。修饰言行,不修饰人。

items.zh: 咬紧牙关接受(不得不做的痛苦决定)
items.en: to force yourself to accept something unpleasant because there is no better option
items.example: After two years of deferrals the council had to bite the bullet and close the two least-used libraries.
items.note: 强调"明知痛苦但躲不掉";不等于单纯的"下决心",那是 make up one's mind。

items.zh: 试图一口气解决过于庞大的问题;贪大求全
items.en: to attempt something impossibly large in scope when a narrower effort would actually work
items.example: Our lead engineer told the team not to boil the ocean: pick three broken endpoints and ship fixes by Friday.
items.note: 咨询业与科技业行话,几乎总以否定形式出现(let's not boil the ocean)。字面「把海煮开」完全猜不出来。

items.zh: 把最关键的信息埋在后面;讲话抓不住重点
items.en: to place the most important fact far down in a piece instead of at the start
items.example: You buried the lede — the outage lasted nine hours, and that belongs in the first line, not paragraph six.
items.note: lede 是新闻业为区别于铅字 lead 而改的拼法,专指导语;拼成 lead 也可以。现在早已扩用到日常讲话和邮件。

items.zh: 影响长期挥之不去
items.en: to go on affecting things long afterwards
items.example: The 1998 default still casts a long shadow over how the country's bonds are priced today.
items.note: 后接 over / on;基本只用于负面的持续影响,不用来夸功绩。

items.zh: 抱团自保:组织内部一致对外、拒绝外部质询
items.en: to close ranks defensively as a group when facing outside criticism or scrutiny
items.example: Instead of answering the auditor's questions, the leadership team circled the wagons and routed every request through legal.
items.note: 美国西部拓荒时马车围成圈防御。含贬义,暗示封闭、心虚,不是褒义的「团结」。

items.zh: (同一理由或事实)对双方都成立;是把双刃剑
items.en: to have two opposite effects, or to support both sides of an argument equally
items.example: Transparency cuts both ways: the same disclosure rules that expose the supplier also let competitors read our margins.
items.note: 主语是论点、政策、特质,不能是人——不是「两面派」。中文的「双刃剑」偏重坏处,英文纯粹指「两边都适用」。

items.zh: 偷工减料;为省时省钱而降低标准
items.en: to save time or money by skipping steps that should not be skipped
items.example: The inquiry found that the contractor cut corners on fire testing to keep the tower's cladding within budget.
items.note: 贬义,指为省钱省时牺牲质量或安全,不是中性的"抄近路"。

items.zh: 无人理会;充耳不闻
items.en: to be ignored by the people with the power to act
items.example: Three years of memos from the safety inspector fell on deaf ears until the roof of the warehouse collapsed.
items.note: 主语是警告、请求本身而非人;暗示对方是不肯听,不是听不见。

items.zh: 害人反害己;被自己设的局反噬
items.en: harmed by the very scheme, rule, or weapon one devised to harm others
items.example: The senator who wrote the strict disclosure law was hoist by his own petard when reporters filed a request about his own trades.
items.note: 物主代词随主语变(her / their / your own petard)。petard 是古代炸城门的火药包,hoist 是古过去分词「被炸上天」,两词今天都只活在这个短语里。出自莎士比亚(原文用 with),现多见于评论文章的挖苦语气。

items.zh: (说法、论点)站得住脚,经得起推敲
items.en: to stand up to scrutiny; to be logically sound
items.example: His explanation that the server logs were deleted automatically doesn't hold water, because retention was set to ninety days.
items.note: 九成以上出现在否定句里(doesn't hold water)。主语必须是论点、借口、理论,不能是人。

items.headword: kick the can down the road
items.zh: 把问题往后拖;拖延而不解决
items.en: to postpone dealing with a problem instead of resolving it
items.example: Rather than raise contributions before the election, the government chose to kick the can down the road for another four years.
items.note: 政治与财政报道的固定说法,带明显批评意味;比 postpone 多了"回避责任"的暗示。

items.zh: 先粗略查验一下;在决定前非正式地试试深浅
items.en: to give something a quick, informal inspection before committing to it
items.example: Two buyers came by to kick the tires on the warehouse, but neither asked to see the roof survey.
items.note: 来自买二手车时踢踢轮胎。强调「初步、随手看看」,与正式尽职调查恰恰相反。

items.zh: 低垂的果实;最容易拿到的成果
items.en: the easiest gains available, taken before the harder work begins
items.example: The first ten per cent of emissions cuts was low-hanging fruit; insulating older housing stock will cost ten times as much.
items.note: 不可数,不说 a low-hanging fruit;常出现在"容易的部分已经做完了"这个语境。

items.zh: 中途改变评判标准,让对方永远达不到要求
items.en: to change the criteria for success after someone has already started trying to meet them
items.example: Every time we hit the agreed metrics, the client moved the goalposts and asked for a fourth round of revisions.
items.note: 是指控对方不讲信用,不是中性的「调整目标」。足球来源,但美式英语用得同样多。

items.zh: 产生实质性影响;明显改变局面
items.en: to have a noticeable effect on a situation or a measurable outcome
items.example: A quarter-point cut will not move the needle on housing affordability when the shortage is one of supply, not credit.
items.note: 商业与政策报道里的高频说法,常见于否定式 won't/doesn't move the needle;比 have a significant effect 自然得多。

items.zh: 把水搅浑:引入无关信息,使本来清楚的事变得难以判断
items.en: to make an issue harder to judge by introducing confusing or irrelevant material
items.example: The defense muddied the waters by introducing three unrelated timelines, and the jury spent a day untangling dates.
items.note: 与中文「把水搅浑」几乎完全对应,但英文不一定含故意——笨拙的解释也能 muddy the waters。

items.zh: 粉饰问题;做表面功夫掩盖根本缺陷
items.en: to hide a fundamental problem with a superficial fix
items.example: The emergency credit line will paper over the cracks, but the bank's funding model is still short by a third.
items.note: 英式用法更常见;强调"糊住裂缝"而不是修好它。

items.zh: 意料之中的常态(通常指坏事)
items.en: exactly what you would expect in the circumstances, usually something unwelcome
items.example: A two-hour wait at the licensing office is par for the course, and the staff no longer bother apologising.
items.note: 出自高尔夫,语气是无奈的接受;几乎只用于不好的事,不用于夸奖。

items.zh: 口惠而实不至;嘴上支持却不落实
items.en: to express support for something publicly while doing nothing to advance it
items.example: Both parties pay lip service to rail investment, yet neither has funded a single new line north of the capital.
items.note: 强烈贬义;固定形式 pay lip service to + 名词,不能说 speak 或 give lip service。

items.zh: 叫停;撤资停掉(项目、资助)
items.en: to stop supporting or funding something, ending it abruptly
items.example: If subscriber growth stalls a third quarter running, the board will pull the plug on the studio's original films.
items.note: 后接 on;主语通常是掌握资金或权力的一方,不是执行者自己。

items.headword: put a thumb on the scale
items.zh: 暗中做手脚使结果偏向一方;吃里扒外地偏袒
items.en: to quietly interfere so that a supposedly neutral process favours one side
items.example: The regulator is supposed to stay neutral, yet the revised formula quietly puts a thumb on the scale for incumbent carriers.
items.note: 来自小贩称重时偷按秤盘。专指本应中立的一方(裁判、监管者、平台)偷偷偏袒,普通人偏心不用它。

items.zh: 繁文缛节;官僚手续
items.en: excessive official procedure that slows things down
items.example: Clinics said the grant was welcome but the red tape around it consumed a nurse's time for a fortnight.
items.note: 不可数,不说 a red tape 或 red tapes;比 bureaucracy 更带抱怨语气。

items.zh: 走过场式批准;不加审查地照批
items.en: to approve something formally and automatically, without real scrutiny
items.example: The supervisory board rubber-stamped the chief executive's pay package in under ten minutes, with no questions from the floor.
items.note: 贬义,强调只是盖章、没有实质审查;名词形式 a rubber stamp 可指这样的机构。

items.zh: 迁怒于报信人;把坏消息的传达者当成责任人
items.en: to blame the person who delivers bad news rather than the situation the news describes
items.example: Don't shoot the messenger, but the lab says the samples were contaminated before they ever reached our freezer.
items.note: 最常见的是否定祈使 don't shoot the messenger——说话人先给自己撇清,表示「我只是转达」。

items.zh: 自身押上了真金白银的利害关系,而非旁观者
items.en: a personal stake — usually money or risk — in the outcome one is advocating
items.example: The founders each put in two years of salary, so nobody could claim they had no skin in the game.
items.note: 金融与管理写作高频,固定搭配 have / no skin in the game。核心是「输了自己也疼」,不只是「关心」。

items.zh: 真正的检验;试金石
items.en: the decisive trial that shows whether something really works
items.example: The acid test is not the demo but next January, when four thousand nurses log in at once.
items.note: 源自验金,含义是"过了这关才算数";比 the real test 更有分量。

items.zh: 预警信号:最先出问题、预示更大危机的那一环
items.en: an early indicator whose failure warns that a wider crisis is coming
items.example: Independent bookshops are the canary in the coal mine for a high street; when they close, the chains follow within two years.
items.note: 矿工带金丝雀下井探毒气。重点是「预警」而非「牺牲品」——用错成后者是常见误用。

items.zh: 房间里的大象;人人都看得见却都不愿提的问题
items.en: an obvious, serious problem that everyone present avoids mentioning
items.example: Three hours of restructuring talk went by before anyone named the elephant in the room: the pension deficit nobody wanted to fund.
items.note: 常搭配 address / name / ignore the elephant in the room。

items.headword: the exception that proves the rule
items.zh: 被明文列出的例外,恰恰证明存在一条通则
items.en: an explicitly stated exception that implies a general rule covering all the cases it does not cover
items.example: The notice reading "no parking on Sundays" is the exception that proves the rule: every other day, parking is clearly permitted.
items.note: prove 在这里是古义「检验、证实……的存在」。通俗用法把任何反例都说成「证明了规则」,逻辑上讲不通,却连母语者也天天这么用——自己写作时按严格义用。

items.zh: 尚无定论;还看不出结论
items.en: no conclusion has been reached yet because the evidence is not in
items.example: Two trials showed a benefit and one showed none, so the jury is still out on whether the drug slows decline.
items.note: 后接 on;比 it is not clear yet 地道得多,常用于科学与政策评估。

items.zh: 最大的那一份;绝大部分
items.en: much the largest part of something being divided
items.example: Three cloud providers take the lion's share of the market, leaving the rest to split what is barely a tenth.
items.note: 指"最大的一份",不一定过半;后面固定接 of。

items.zh: 本末倒置;次要环节反过来支配了主要目标
items.en: a situation where a minor part controls the whole, reversing the proper order of importance
items.example: Compliance now dictates which products we launch, which feels like the tail wagging the dog to everyone on the design floor.
items.note: 最接近「本末倒置」,但英文强调的是「小的那个在操控大的那个」。常用完整句式 a case of the tail wagging the dog。

items.zh: 开口子;看似轻微的第一步,却会引出严重得多的后果
items.en: a small change that seems harmless but opens the way to much larger and unwelcome ones
items.example: Charging for checked bags looked minor, but frequent flyers called it the thin end of the wedge, and seat fees followed.
items.note: 英式为主;美式同义常说 slippery slope。楔子是「薄的一头先进去」,不是「结局很薄弱」。

items.zh: 冰山一角
items.en: the small visible part of a much larger hidden problem
items.example: The four cases that reached court were the tip of the iceberg; the regulator's own audit counted more than two hundred.
items.note: 冠词 the 不能省;常写作 only / just the tip of the iceberg。

items.zh: 不祥之兆;败局已定的征兆
items.en: clear signs that something is about to fail or end
items.example: Two of the three founders had already sold their stakes, so the staff could see the writing on the wall.
items.note: 常搭配 see / read / ignore;只用于坏结局,不能说好事的征兆。

items.zh: 为挽回已亏的投入而继续追加投入,结果亏得更多
items.en: to spend more on a failing venture in the hope of recovering what has already been lost
items.example: After two failed rewrites, the board refused to throw good money after bad and shut the platform down in March.
items.note: good / bad 说的是钱本身——「还没打水漂的钱」和「已经打水漂的钱」,与道德无关。对应沉没成本谬误。

items.zh: 姑且听之;对某说法持保留态度
items.en: with scepticism, treating a claim as possibly exaggerated
items.example: Investors took the founder's revenue projection with a pinch of salt, given that the previous two had missed by half.
items.note: 美式多说 with a grain of salt;固定动词是 take,不能说 hear/listen with a pinch of salt。

items.zh: 占(比例);说明…的原因
items.en: to make up a particular proportion of a total, or to explain the reason for something
items.example: Rural districts account for barely a tenth of the population but nearly half of the road deaths.
items.note: 课堂上只教"解释"这一义,而在数据写作里"占比"用得更多:X accounts for 30% of Y。

items.zh: 让步,放弃原来坚持的立场
items.en: to withdraw from a position or demand that you were defending
items.example: Neither side would back down over the parking spaces, so the dispute reached the residents' committee.
items.note: back down 是放弃立场;back off 是别再逼近、别插手,两个不能换。

items.zh: 支持,佐证;备份(数据);倒车
items.en: to support someone's claim with evidence, or to make a copy of data
items.example: If the client disputes the timeline, the email thread will back up every date we ever gave them.
items.note: 三个常义靠语境分(声援/备份/倒车);名词形式写成一个词 backup。

items.zh: 一开始就把…做进去、内建进去(成本、假设、限制)
items.en: to build something into a plan, price, or system from the start so that it cannot easily be removed
items.example: The delay was baked in from day one, since nobody seriously expected the permits to arrive on time.
items.note: 商业与技术语境的新兴说法,形象是"烤进面团里,再也挑不出来"。常见被动 be baked in / baked into the price。

items.zh: 证实,印证(说法、担心、预测)
items.en: to confirm that a claim, theory, or fear was correct
items.example: The audit bore out what the junior analyst had flagged in March and everyone had politely ignored.
items.note: 主语是证据,宾语是说法:the data bears out the claim。与 bear"忍受、承担"那一族毫无关系。

items.zh: 触底(并随后回升)
items.en: to reach the lowest point before starting to improve
items.example: House prices bottomed out in March and have crept up every month since, though nobody trusts it yet.
items.note: 含义的重点在"之后会回升";只说跌到最低是 hit a low。用 bottom out 等于给了一个乐观判断。

items.zh: 提起(话题);抚养(孩子)
items.en: to raise a topic in conversation; also, to raise a child
items.example: Nobody wanted to bring up the missing receipts while the founder was still sitting in the room.
items.note: mention 是中性的"提到",bring up 暗示主动把话题挑起来。

items.zh: 不予理会,轻描淡写地打发掉
items.en: to dismiss a person or a concern without giving it serious attention
items.example: The manager tried to brush off the safety complaint as nerves, and the inspector wrote it into the report.
items.note: 重点在"没当回事就打发了";名词 the brush-off 指吃闭门羹。

items.zh: 认同、接受(某种说法)
items.en: to accept an idea or explanation, often uncritically
items.example: Half the newsroom bought into the leak before anyone checked whether the document had a plausible sender.
items.note: 除字面的"买入股份"外,更常见的是"买账";否定式 not buy into 语气很重。

items.zh: 取消,叫停(已安排好的活动)
items.en: to cancel an event, or to stop an activity that is already under way
items.example: Organizers had to call off the parade an hour before it started when the wind gusts hit fifty.
items.note: cancel 是通用词;call off 更强调临时叫停已经在进行或已排定的事。

items.zh: 执行,实施(命令、检查、研究)
items.en: to perform or complete a task, an order, or a piece of research
items.example: Inspectors carry out spot checks at the port twice a month, usually before dawn to catch the night shift.
items.note: 美式书面常用 conduct,但 carry out orders/a study/an attack 是通用搭配。

items.zh: 结转,顺延到下一个周期
items.en: to transfer something unused from one period into the next
items.example: Only five leave days carry over into the new year; the rest vanish at midnight on December thirty-first.
items.note: 假期、预算、亏损都能 carry over。名词 carryover 在财务报表里就是"结转"。

items.zh: 流行起来;(终于)反应过来
items.en: to become popular, or to finally understand something
items.example: The refill scheme took two years to catch on, and now three supermarkets on the street copy it.
items.note: become popular 太长,母语者说 catch on;第二义"开窍了"也常用。

items.zh: 顶不住而屈服;(屋顶、地面)塌陷
items.en: to give way under pressure, or of a roof or wall, to collapse inward
items.example: The union expected management to cave in by Friday, but the offer on the table never moved.
items.note: 比 give in 更狠,暗示"撑不住了";字面义是塌方。

items.zh: 一点一点削弱,蚕食
items.en: to gradually reduce or weaken something through many small actions
items.example: Small monthly fees chip away at the deposit until tenants get back barely half of what they paid.
items.note: 强调蚕食式的缓慢消耗,宾语常是信任、优势、存款、领先。

items.zh: 凑钱,出份子;搭把手
items.en: to contribute money or effort along with other people
items.example: Everyone on the floor agreed to chip in ten pounds for the leaving present and the card.
items.note: 小额凑份子的固定说法;这种场合用 contribute 会显得很生硬。

items.zh: 机械地大批量炮制(常暗示质量不高)
items.en: to produce something rapidly and in large quantities, often without much care
items.example: The site churns out thirty listicles a day, and you can tell which twenty-nine were written before lunch.
items.note: 几乎总是贬义:量大、快、粗糙。夸人高产要用 prolific,不能用 churn out。

items.zh: 回心转意,想通了;(昏迷后)苏醒
items.en: to change your mind and accept something, or to regain consciousness
items.example: Her father took a year to come around to the idea of a daughter driving lorries for a living.
items.note: 英式常拼作 come round;"想通"义后面接 to the idea of。

items.zh: 弄到手(尤指不容易得到的东西)
items.en: to obtain something, especially something that is hard to get
items.example: Honest feedback is hard to come by once you are the one signing everyone's timesheets.
items.note: 最高频的形式就是 hard to come by(难得)。带宾语时才是"弄到";不带宾语的 come by 是"顺路过来一趟"。

items.zh: 归根结底是……的问题
items.en: to be, in the end, a question of one essential thing
items.example: Strip away the rhetoric and the dispute comes down to who pays for the pipeline's last forty kilometres.
items.note: 常用来收束论证:"说到底就是……";后接名词或 wh- 从句。

items.zh: 想出,提出(办法、点子、名字)
items.en: to produce an idea, plan, or solution, especially under pressure
items.example: The two of them had one night to come up with a name the trademark office would actually approve.
items.note: 学习者常写 propose/devise;"临时想出个办法"在英语里就是 come up with。

items.zh: 指望,依靠
items.en: to rely on someone or something with confidence
items.example: Growers here count on one week of dry weather in September, and this year it never came.
items.note: rely on 的口语版;you can count on it 意思是"这事儿准跑不了"。

items.zh: 严厉打击,整顿
items.en: to start taking strict action against a behaviour or group
items.example: The city plans to crack down on unlicensed rentals after a fire in a converted attic last winter.
items.note: 几乎总接 on;名词写作一个词 crackdown,是新闻标题常客。

items.zh: 挤占,排挤掉(资源、空间、其他参与者)
items.en: to take up so much of something that other things cannot get any
items.example: Short-term rentals crowded out long-term tenants until the council capped licences at three hundred per district.
items.note: 经济学"挤出效应"(crowding out)的日常版。主语不是存心排挤的人,而是占了位子的那样东西。

items.zh: 削减,缩减(开支、用量)
items.en: to reduce spending, consumption, or activity
items.example: The council will cut back on street cleaning before it touches the libraries, or so the leaflet claims.
items.note: 常接 on;名词写作 cutback。比 reduce 口语化。

items.zh: (某事)让某人恍然明白过来
items.en: to become suddenly clear to someone after a period of not realising it
items.example: Halfway to the airport it dawned on me that my passport was still on the kitchen table.
items.note: 主语是事情,宾语才是人,与中文语序相反:it dawned on me that…。不能说 I dawned on it。

items.zh: 废除,取消(制度、规定、习惯)
items.en: to abolish something or get rid of it, especially a rule or a practice
items.example: The school voted to do away with the uniform tie, and half the parents wrote in that same week.
items.note: abolish 的口语版,宾语多是制度和惯例,不用于具体物品。

items.zh: 变本加厉地坚持(尤指在已经出问题的立场上加码)
items.en: to commit even more strongly to a course of action, especially a risky or failing one
items.example: Instead of apologising, the brand doubled down on the campaign and bought a second round of billboards.
items.note: 出自二十一点的"加倍下注"。多含贬义:明知不妙还往里投。常搭 double down on。

items.zh: 借助,调用(经验、储备、资金)
items.en: to use a supply of something such as experience, savings, or resources that you have available
items.example: She drew on twenty years in emergency medicine to keep the whole ward calm during the six-hour power cut.
items.note: 宾语必须是"可支取的储备":experience / savings / reserves。与"在…上画画"的字面义靠搭配区分。

items.zh: 老想着,揪住不放(多指不快的事)
items.en: to keep thinking or talking about something, usually something unpleasant
items.example: The coach refused to dwell on the missed penalty and started the next drill within a minute.
items.note: 语气偏负面,暗示"不该一直纠结"。

items.zh: 把…算进去,计入考虑
items.en: to include something as a consideration when calculating or deciding
items.example: The estimate looks cheap until you factor in the ferry crossing and two nights of accommodation.
items.note: consider 太笼统;factor in 强调把某项成本或变量"算进公式里"。

items.zh: 退而依靠(备用办法)
items.en: to resort to something dependable after the preferred option fails
items.example: With the new database offline, the clerks fell back on the paper ledgers they had been told to shred.
items.note: 隐含"这不是首选";英式写作也作 fall back upon,意思相同。

items.zh: (计划、交易)落空,告吹
items.en: of a plan or deal, to fail to happen after it had seemed likely
items.example: The bank sat on the paperwork for a month and let the whole house sale fall through.
items.note: 主语只能是计划、交易、婚约这类事,不能是人。

items.zh: 把(工作)外包、转包出去
items.en: to send work out to other people or companies rather than doing it in-house
items.example: The studio farmed out the background animation to a smaller shop in Osaka and kept the character work.
items.note: 比 outsource 口语,而且常带一点"甩包袱"的味道 —— 说自己 farm out 工作不一定好听。

items.zh: 弄明白;想出办法解决
items.en: to work out the answer to something, or to come to understand it
items.example: It took the pharmacist ten minutes to figure out why the two prescriptions kept cancelling each other out.
items.note: "搞懂/搞定"的默认说法;determine、ascertain 在口语里几乎不出现。

items.zh: 充实细节,把粗略的东西做具体
items.en: to add detail to an outline or rough idea so that it becomes complete
items.example: The pitch was two slides and a slogan; they spent the weekend fleshing out the numbers behind it.
items.note: flesh 是"肉":骨架已有,往上添肉。注意别写成 flash out,那是另一回事。

items.zh: 把事情做到底,把承诺落实
items.en: to complete something you started or promised, all the way to the end
items.example: Plenty of departments announce a recycling policy; far fewer follow through once the bins need emptying.
items.note: 常接 on。follow through 是有始有终,follow up 只是后续跟进一次。

items.zh: 把成本或工作量集中安排在前期
items.en: to concentrate cost, effort, or benefit at the beginning of a period rather than spreading it evenly
items.example: They front-loaded the course with grammar, so the first month felt brutal and the last one felt like a holiday.
items.note: 项目管理与财务的常用词,反义是 back-load。中文没有对应的单个词,所以学习者几乎不会主动说出来。

items.zh: 绕过(规定、障碍);四处走动出行
items.en: to find a way past an obstacle or rule; also, to move from place to place
items.example: Firms get around the cap by splitting one contract into three, and the current wording allows it.
items.note: 第三义 get around to sth 是"总算抽空去做",与前两义完全不同。

items.zh: 想说的是…,言下之意是
items.en: to be trying to say or imply something, often indirectly
items.example: After twenty minutes I finally understood what he was getting at: the whole department was being moved.
items.note: 高频形式 what are you getting at?(你到底想说什么?)语气偏不耐烦。英式口语里还有"针对、找茬"一义。

items.zh: 做了坏事却未受惩罚,蒙混过关
items.en: to do something wrong and escape punishment or criticism for it
items.example: For six years the firm managed to get away with billing hours that nobody had actually worked.
items.note: 中文"逃过一劫、没被追究";英语里没有更简洁的单词能替代。

items.zh: (从疾病、打击中)恢复过来
items.en: to recover from an illness, a shock, or a disappointment
items.example: It took him a full term to get over the flu and another to get back onto the team.
items.note: 用于病痛、失恋、打击;"克服困难"更常说 overcome,别混。

items.zh: 让步,屈服(停止抵抗)
items.en: to stop resisting and accept what someone else wants
items.example: After three nights of the dog howling next door, the neighbours give in and let it sleep indoors.
items.note: give in 是向压力让步,give up 是放弃某事,学习者最常混这一对。

items.zh: 一笔带过,含糊掩饰(尴尬的事实)
items.en: to deal with an awkward fact so quickly that it attracts little attention
items.example: The annual report tends to gloss over the two quarters when the warehouse stood almost completely empty.
items.note: 不是撒谎,而是"轻轻带过";几乎总是批评性用法。

items.zh: 反复讨论直到谈拢(细节、条款)
items.en: to discuss something at length until the details are agreed
items.example: The two teams hashed out the handover schedule over four hours and a whiteboard covered in arrows.
items.note: 强调过程冗长费劲,但最后有结论。与 iron out 的分工:hash out 是从零谈出细节,iron out 是抹平剩下的分歧。

items.zh: 抢先阻止(坏事发生),拦截
items.en: to prevent something bad from happening by acting before it does
items.example: A quick apology on Friday headed off a complaint that would have reached the regulator by Monday.
items.note: 不是"出发前往" —— 那个义项后面必须跟地点(head off to Rome)。带宾语时一律是"抢先拦住"。

items.zh: 完全取决于(某一决定性因素)
items.en: to depend entirely on one decisive factor
items.example: The whole prosecution hinges on a single receipt, and the defence has spent three days attacking it.
items.note: 比 depend on 重得多:是"成败全系于此",不是一般意义的依赖。

items.zh: 忍住;隐瞒(信息);拖后腿
items.en: to restrain something or someone, or to keep information to yourself
items.example: The witness chose to hold back one detail, and the whole timeline collapsed at the second hearing.
items.note: 三义常见:忍住眼泪 / 瞒着不说 / 妨碍某人发展。

items.zh: 经得起检验,站得住脚
items.en: to remain valid or convincing when examined closely
items.example: The alibi did not hold up: the café had CCTV, and he was not in any frame that evening.
items.note: 学习者一般只学到"举起、耽搁、抢劫"。"经得起推敲"这一义在法律与学术语境极常见:hold up in court / under scrutiny。

items.zh: 解决(剩下的分歧、小问题)
items.en: to resolve the remaining difficulties or disagreements in something
items.example: The two sides met on Sunday to iron out the last three clauses before the deadline at noon.
items.note: 只用于"最后那点小疙瘩",不用于根本性冲突。

items.zh: 裁员(因业务收缩,非因过失)
items.en: to dismiss workers because there is not enough work, not because of their performance
items.example: The plant will lay off ninety people in March, and the town's only diner is already bracing for it.
items.note: 与 fire(因过失开除)严格区分,混用会得罪人;名词是 layoff。

items.zh: 调查,了解一下(某件事)
items.en: to investigate a matter in order to find out the facts
items.example: The regulator promised to look into the billing errors, and three months later nothing had been published.
items.note: investigate 的日常版,语气更轻,不一定是正式立案。

items.zh: 造就,导致(某种效果或局面)
items.en: to result in or contribute to a particular outcome
items.example: Two strong personalities on one small team make for lively meetings and painfully slow decisions.
items.note: 评论文章里的常见句式:makes for a good story / makes for uncomfortable reading。另一义"朝…走去"后面必须跟地点。

items.zh: 对…作何理解,怎么看待
items.en: to form a particular opinion or interpretation of something
items.example: I still don't know what to make of her email; it was four lines long and signed with her full name.
items.note: 几乎固定在 what to make of / what do you make of 之中。不是"用…做成" —— 那是 be made of。

items.zh: 勉强辨认出(看清、听清、认出)
items.en: to manage to see, hear, or understand something with difficulty
items.example: Through the rain I could just make out the number on the bus, and it was the wrong one.
items.note: 教材几乎不教这个"勉强辨认"的义项,而它在日常叙述里最常用。另有美式俚语义"亲热",别用错场合。

items.zh: 磕磕绊绊地对付过去(没章法但最终勉强完成)
items.en: to manage to get through something despite having no clear plan or proper preparation
items.example: Neither of us spoke Portuguese, so we muddled through the market with hand gestures and a screenshot of the address.
items.note: 说自己 muddle through 是自嘲和谦虚;说别人则是在指其毫无章法。语气差别全看主语是谁。

items.zh: 反复琢磨,慢慢考虑
items.en: to think about something carefully over a period of time
items.example: He asked for the weekend to mull over the transfer before giving the school a final answer.
items.note: 比 consider 多一层"慢慢想"的时间感,常配 for a few days。

items.zh: 承认(自己犯的错)
items.en: to admit that you were the one who did something wrong
items.example: Two weeks passed before the intern would own up to deleting the entire shared drive folder.
items.note: 常接 to:own up to doing sth。语气比 confess 轻,适合小过失。

items.zh: 粉饰,掩盖(矛盾或裂痕),而非真正解决
items.en: to hide a disagreement or flaw superficially instead of dealing with it
items.example: The joint statement papered over a split that everyone in the room had watched widen all afternoon.
items.note: 常搭 paper over the cracks。重点在"只贴了层纸",问题还在下面 —— 用它就是在暗示这种掩盖迟早要破。

items.zh: 渐渐减弱直至消失
items.en: to dwindle gradually until nothing is left
items.example: The protest filled the square for a fortnight, then petered out once the rain came and the cameras left.
items.note: 强调"慢慢没了声息"而非戛然而止;主语多为势头、谈判、线索。

items.zh: 分阶段淘汰,逐步停用
items.en: to stop using or providing something gradually, in planned stages
items.example: The city is phasing out diesel buses, replacing about forty a year until the last one retires in 2031.
items.note: 关键在"分阶段";一刀切叫 scrap 或 ban。反义 phase in(逐步引入)同样常用。

items.zh: 淡化,把事情说得没那么严重
items.en: to make something seem less important or serious than it really is
items.example: Officials tried to play down the leak until a second village reported the same taste in its water.
items.note: 新闻里高频;反义是 play up(渲染)。单词形式 downplay 同义。

items.zh: 指出(别人没注意到的事实)
items.en: to draw attention to a fact, especially one that others have missed
items.example: Someone in the back row had to point out that the chart's two axes were labelled the same.
items.note: 书面里 note/indicate 更正式;口头指出别人的疏漏基本都用 point out。

items.zh: 因价格过高而把…挤出(市场、地段)
items.en: to make something so expensive that a group of people can no longer afford it
items.example: Two new towers priced out the families who had rented on that street for a generation.
items.note: 常用被动 be priced out of。注意同形的另一义:price something out 是"报价、算成本",靠上下文区分。

items.zh: 成功做成(本来很难的事)
items.en: to succeed at something difficult, against expectations
items.example: Nobody thought a two-person team could pull off a launch in six weeks, but the demo ran clean.
items.note: 自带"本来悬,居然成了"的语气;achieve 完全没有这层意思。

items.zh: 顶回去,提出反对;把日期往后推
items.en: to resist or object to a plan or instruction; also, to move a date later
items.example: Expect the ward staff to push back on any rota written without asking a single one of them first.
items.note: 近十年职场英语里的高频词;名词 pushback 指来自内部的阻力。

items.zh: 推迟,拖延(尤指因为不想面对)
items.en: to postpone something, especially because you would rather not face it
items.example: They put off the safety audit twice, and by the third delay the inspector stopped answering emails.
items.note: 母语者日常说 put off;postpone 其实偏正式书面,口语里很少听到。

items.zh: 忍受,容忍(不愉快的人或事)
items.en: to tolerate something unpleasant without trying to stop it
items.example: She put up with the landlord's excuses for a year before finally filing a complaint with the housing board.
items.note: tolerate/endure 太书面;抱怨语气的"忍"几乎都是 put up with。

items.zh: 被使唤、被占便宜(而自己又不好意思拒绝)
items.en: to be taken advantage of by someone who keeps asking you for favours
items.example: She started to feel put upon: every weekend shift somehow became hers, and nobody ever asked twice.
items.note: 几乎只以被动出现:feel put upon / be put upon。upon 不能换成 on —— put on 是完全另一个词。

items.zh: 勒住,收紧,加以约束(开支、权力、脾气)
items.en: to bring something under control by limiting it
items.example: The new chief reined in travel spending, and suddenly nobody was flying to Frankfurt for a ninety-minute meeting.
items.note: rein 是缰绳,不是 reign(统治) —— 这个拼写错母语者也常犯。搭配:rein in spending / costs / ambition。

items.zh: 挺过,熬过(风暴、危机、低谷)
items.en: to survive a difficult period without being destroyed by it
items.example: The bakery rode out two lockdowns on savings, then reopened with half the staff and twice the queue.
items.note: 源自航海:骑着浪头挺过风暴。重点不是解决问题,而是不做大动作、撑到它自己过去。

items.zh: 撤销,回退(政策、涨价、已生效的改动)
items.en: to reverse or reduce something that was previously introduced
items.example: The airline rolled back the baggage fee within a week, once the screenshots started trending.
items.note: 与 walk back 的分工:roll back 撤的是已经生效的政策或价格,walk back 撤的只是说过的话。

items.zh: 排除(某种可能性或嫌疑)
items.en: to eliminate something as a possibility
items.example: Doctors could not rule out an infection until the second culture came back forty-eight hours later.
items.note: 不同于泛指的 exclude,rule out 专指排除可能性,医学与新闻里极常见。

items.zh: 达到,总计(某数量、篇幅、金额)
items.en: to amount to or extend to a particular quantity, length, or cost
items.example: The judgment runs to four hundred pages, and the part everyone quotes is a footnote on page three.
items.note: 不是"跑向"。书面英语里这个"总计达到"的义项很常见:the bill ran to、the report runs to。

items.zh: 看穿(谎言、伪装);坚持到底
items.en: to recognize that someone or something is deceptive; also, to continue with something until it is finished
items.example: Any decent auditor would see through invoices dated on a Sunday for a warehouse that shuts at noon.
items.note: 两义都常见;"坚持到底"义中间要插代词:see it through。

items.zh: (书面)阐明,载明;着手去做
items.en: to state or explain something formally in writing
items.example: The terms are set out in clause nine, which nobody reads until the relationship has already gone wrong.
items.note: 合同与报告的固定说法 as set out in / set out below。学习者通常只知道"出发",而书面语里"载明"这一义更常遇到。

items.zh: 支撑,加固(摇摇欲坠的信心、财务、联盟)
items.en: to support or strengthen something that is at risk of failing
items.example: The central bank cut rates again to shore up confidence, but the currency slid another two percent by Friday.
items.note: shore 在这里是"支撑柱",不是"海岸"。财经新闻高频:shore up support / confidence / finances。

items.zh: 出现,到场(尤指本来不确定会不会来)
items.en: to arrive or appear somewhere, especially when attendance was uncertain
items.example: Only four of the twelve volunteers show up on rainy Saturdays, so the coordinator now over-recruits every week.
items.note: 比 appear/attend 口语得多;"人没来"日常就说 didn't show up。

items.zh: 对……不以为然;轻松扛过
items.en: to dismiss something as unimportant, or to recover from it easily
items.example: The chairman shrugged off the resignation letters as routine turnover, then cancelled every meeting for the rest of the week.
items.note: 既指"不当回事",也指经济、伤病"轻松挺过";用在人身上常暗含作者的怀疑。

items.zh: 正式批准,签字认可
items.en: to give formal approval to something
items.example: Nobody would sign off on the budget until the legal team had read the indemnity clause twice.
items.note: 三个词缺一不可:sign off(不带 on)是"收尾、下班、结束通话";加了 on 才是"批准"。

items.zh: 单独挑出(点名批评或特别表扬)
items.en: to select one person or thing from a group for special attention
items.example: The report did not single out any one department, but everyone knew which floor it meant.
items.note: 不是中性的 choose,而是从一群人里"拎出来说事"。

items.zh: 压着不办;故意扣住(报告、消息、申请)
items.en: to deliberately delay acting on something, or to keep information from being released
items.example: Legal sat on the report for three weeks, and by the time it surfaced the deadline for appeal had passed.
items.note: 字面"坐在上面"就是形象来源:不是忘了,是有意压着。指责意味很强,写正式邮件时慎用。

items.zh: 说明、印证(某一点);针对某议题发言
items.en: to be evidence of something, or to address a particular point
items.example: The fact that three of her former interns now run their own labs speaks to how she trained people.
items.note: 这里主语是事实或证据,不是人,所以跟"和某人说话"完全不同:speaks to his character / speaks to the wider problem。

items.zh: 讲清楚,明确写明(不留推测空间)
items.en: to explain something in explicit detail, leaving nothing to inference
items.example: The contract does not spell out who pays for shipping, which is exactly where the argument started.
items.note: 常隐含"条文没写明"或"对方还没听懂",带一点不耐烦。

items.zh: 分拆(业务)使其独立;衍生出
items.en: to separate part of a company or project so that it becomes independent
items.example: They spun off the payments unit last spring, and it is now worth more than the parent company.
items.note: 名词 spin-off 中文多译"衍生剧",但动词形式绝大多数出现在企业分拆的财经语境。

items.zh: 把…办妥,安排停当
items.en: to finish or settle something so that it no longer needs attention
items.example: Once we square away the visa paperwork, the whole team can fly out on the Sunday flight.
items.note: 美式口语,最常见的是被动 get something squared away。square 在这里是动词"摆正",与"平方、广场"无关。

items.zh: 容忍(多用于否定);代表,象征
items.en: to tolerate something, usually in the negative; also to represent
items.example: The head teacher made it clear she would not stand for phones in the exam hall, ever.
items.note: "代表"那一义人人都会;I won't stand for it(我绝不容忍)这一义几乎没人教,而口语里很常听到。

items.zh: 源于;由……引起
items.en: to have something as its origin or underlying cause
items.example: Most of the delays stem from a single unstaffed customs desk at the border, not from the weather.
items.note: 严肃写作里比 be caused by 更常见;主语通常是问题、分歧这类抽象名词。

items.zh: 承担(工作);雇用;对抗(强敌)
items.en: to accept a responsibility, to hire someone, or to confront a stronger opponent
items.example: A firm of eleven people agreed to take on a case against a hospital trust and its insurers.
items.note: 三义都高频:接活儿 / 招人 / 硬碰硬,全靠宾语判断。

items.zh: 接管,接手(职位、控制权)
items.en: to assume control of something from someone else
items.example: Her deputy will take over the ward on Monday, three days before the inspection team arrives.
items.note: 名词 takeover 专指收购;动词短语泛指各种"接手"。

items.zh: 占用(时间、空间);开始从事(爱好)
items.en: to occupy time or space, or to start doing a new activity
items.example: The new filing cabinets take up half the corridor, so the fire marshal wants them gone by Friday.
items.note: 另一常义是 take up pottery/running,"开始学某项活动",两义都高频。

items.zh: 用居高临下的口气对…说话
items.en: to speak to someone as if they were less intelligent than you
items.example: The consultant talked down to the nurses all morning, explaining their own ward to them in a slow, patient voice.
items.note: 不是"把话说简单点",也不是压价。它指的纯是姿态:内容对不对无所谓,难听的是那副俯视的口吻。

items.zh: 利用,挖掘(市场、情绪、资源)
items.en: to make use of an existing resource, market, or feeling
items.example: The campaign managed to tap into a resentment about parking that had been simmering for a decade.
items.note: 宾语多是尚未被开发的东西:市场、情绪、人才库、资金池。

items.zh: 逐渐减少,慢慢停下来
items.en: to become gradually less in amount or intensity until it stops
items.example: Applications tapered off after the fee went up, from ninety a week to barely a dozen by autumn.
items.note: 强调曲线是慢慢变细,不是断崖式下跌。停药、降雨、需求、热度都常用它。

items.zh: 为…做好铺垫,把事情摆到位只待启动
items.en: to prepare something so that it is ready to happen or to be dealt with
items.example: Her opening question teed up the whole debate, and the minister never recovered from it.
items.note: 来自高尔夫"把球放上球座"。重点是"摆好、只差最后一击",不等于"开始做"。

items.zh: 老调重弹地搬出(用滥了的理由、说法)
items.en: to produce the same tired argument or excuse yet again
items.example: Every budget season they trot out the same chart, and every year somebody points out the axis starts at forty.
items.note: 一定是贬义,暗示这套说辞早听腻了。形象来自把马牵出来遛一圈给人看。

items.zh: 拒绝(邀请、申请);调低(音量、温度)
items.en: to reject an offer or request, or to reduce the level of something
items.example: She had to turn down the fellowship because it started three weeks before her visa cleared.
items.note: 拒绝提议的默认词;decline 更正式,reject 更硬更伤人。

items.zh: 收回,淡化(自己先前的公开表态)
items.en: to retract or soften a public statement you made earlier, usually without admitting you were wrong
items.example: By Thursday the minister was walking back the tax remark, calling it a personal view rather than policy.
items.note: 不是"往回走"。政治与商业新闻的固定用法:话说出去了,再悄悄降调收回,但又不肯认错。

items.zh: 冲淡,削弱(法案、措辞、批评)
items.en: to weaken a proposal, rule, or statement by removing its strongest parts
items.example: Three rounds of amendments water down the bill until the emissions target reads like a polite suggestion.
items.note: 字面是兑水;比喻义在政治与商业报道里比字面义更常见。

items.zh: 逐步收尾、结束(业务、活动);(人)松弛下来
items.en: to gradually bring an activity or business to an end, or to relax after effort
items.example: The charity is winding down after thirty years, and the last shop closes when the lease expires.
items.note: wind 读 /waɪnd/,与"风"无关。两个义项都高频:关掉一门生意,和下班后放松。

items.zh: 核销(坏账);看衰,认定没戏
items.en: to cancel a debt in the accounts, or to dismiss someone or something as hopeless
items.example: Critics were quick to write off the film after its first weekend, and then it ran for eight months.
items.note: 会计义(注销)和口语义(判死刑、看扁)同样高频。
